items.q: Chief advantage of tracheostomy over prolonged translaryngeal intubation beyond about 10 to 14 days is what?
o: Less laryngeal and subglottic injury, better secretion clearance, comfort and weaning
items.exp: Tracheostomy shortens dead space, spares glottis from tube ulceration and stenosis, eases oral care and mobilisation for weaning. Timing individualises by prognosis and anatomy.
r: Incorrect. Cost is not the driver.
Correct. Spares larynx, clears secretions, weans better.
Incorrect. Suction remains essential.
Incorrect. Voice needs fenestration or speaking valve.
items.kp: Two weeks tubed through cords: move the airway below them.

items.q: Emergency cannot intubate cannot oxygenate rescue in adult is which procedure through which landmark?
items.exp: Cricothyroid membrane is palpable even in distorted anatomy and quick to open; formal tracheostomy needs positioning, dissection and time unavailable in hypoxic arrest.
r: Incorrect. Formal tracheostomy is too slow in arrest.
Correct. Membrane rescue, convert later.
Incorrect. Gland surgery is not airway rescue.
Incorrect. Cord injection treats voice, not obstruction.
items.kp: No tube, no oxygen: cut the membrane.

items.q: First tracheostomy tube change is conventionally delayed until about which day and why?
o: About day 5 to 7, after the tract matures
items.exp: A fresh track collapses on tube removal and false passage obstructs; matured fibrous tract guides safe reinsertion, with stay sutures and senior cover for early mishaps.
r: Incorrect. Day one track collapses.
Correct. Mature tract near a week.
Incorrect. Waiting a month invites crusting.
Incorrect. Inner tubes need regular cleaning.
items.kp: Fresh track falls shut: change near day seven.

items.q: Cuff pressure is kept around 20 to 30 cm water chiefly to prevent what?
o: Tracheal mucosal ischaemia, stenosis and fistula from overpressure
items.exp: Capillary perfusion pressure is the ceiling; overinflated cuffs strangulate mucosa circumferentially, scarring into stenosis or eroding neighbours. Underinflation leaks ventilation and aspirates.
r: Incorrect. Speech uses fenestration.
Correct. Overpressure necroses trachea.
Incorrect. Suction clears secretions.
Incorrect. Cough is protective.
items.kp: Cuff harder than capillaries scars the windpipe.

items.q: Small bleed from a tracheostomy stoma three weeks after placement should be treated as what until proven otherwise?
o: Sentinel bleed heralding tracheo innominate fistula, urgent theatre and airway control
items.exp: Low anterior erosion reaches the innominate artery crossing the trachea; herald bleeds precede exsanguination by hours, so massive transfusion, overinflated cuff tamponade and sternotomy capable theatre are mobilised.
r: Incorrect. Timing and site forbid dismissal.
Correct. Sentinel bleed, vessel erosion pathway.
Incorrect. Humidification never excuses bleeding.
Incorrect. Leak changes ventilation, not blood.
items.kp: Late tracheostomy bleed is a vessel warning.

items.q: Classic airway foreign body history in a toddler is which pattern?
o: Gradual wheeze over months both lungs
Sudden choking on peanut, then cough with unilateral wheeze or reduced air entry
Fever and barking cough at midnight
items.exp: Aspiration is abrupt in a well child at play or eating; organic objects lodge bronchially (right favoured) giving asymmetric signs and ball valve trapping. Croup barks febrile at night instead.
r: Incorrect. Gradual bilateral disease is asthma pattern.
Correct. Sudden choke, one quiet side.
Incorrect. That is croup.
Incorrect. Snoring is sleep apnoea territory.
items.kp: Sudden choke, one bad lung: inhaled object.

items.q: Gold standard for suspected bronchial foreign body in a child is what?
o: Rigid bronchoscopy under general anaesthesia for diagnosis and removal
items.exp: Rigid scopes secure ventilation, grasp instruments and control bleeding while extracting varied objects; normal X ray never excludes radiolucent nuts, so clinical suspicion scopes.
r: Incorrect. Physio cannot extract nuts.
Correct. Rigid scope removes under control.
Incorrect. Infection follows retention.
Incorrect. Delay organises granulation.
items.kp: Peanut in airway: rigid scope takes it out.

items.q: Fenestrated tracheostomy tubes assist weaning and speech by what mechanism?
o: Posterior window lets air pass upward through larynx when inner tube removed and cuff deflated
items.exp: Fenestration reconnects upper airway airflow for phonation, cough and capping trials; cuff must be deflated or air cannot pass the seal. Granulation through the window is the classic complication.
r: Incorrect. Cuffs block upward flow.
Correct. Window breathes through voice box.
Incorrect. Suction unchanged.
Incorrect. Length is sizing, not function.
items.kp: Window in tube lets voice box rejoin.

o: Tolerated capping, controlled secretions, safe swallow and resolved original indication
items.exp: Capping trials prove upper airway patency day and night, while swallow and secretion control prevent aspiration after closure; downsizing precedes removal and stoma closes with strapping and observation.
r: Incorrect. Infection delays removal.
Correct. Cap, swallow, dry, cause gone.
Incorrect. Stridor means obstruction persists.
Incorrect. Downsizing, not upsizing, precedes.
items.kp: Cap it, swallow safe, secretions dry: remove.

items.q: Tracheal stenosis after prolonged intubation or cuff injury most often narrows which segment and sounds how?
o: Subglottic or cuff level trachea; biphasic stridor with exertional dyspnoea
items.exp: Fixed narrowing at cricoid or cuff site obstructs both phases (biphasic), mislabelled asthma until flow volume loops flatten and endoscopy grades Cotton Meyer stenosis for dilation or resection.
r: Incorrect. Carina lesions wheeze lower.
Correct. Fixed upper narrowing, both phases.
Incorrect. Crackles are alveolar.
Incorrect. Swallow alone is oesophageal.
items.kp: Both phases noisy after long tubing: cuff scar.
